description: Physical access to and within campus including pathways, buildings, and other spaces; access to opportunity, resources, funding, personnel (including faculty and staff); universal access.
Activism, agency, outreach, civil rights, social justice, Title IX, human rights, LGBTQ rights, program development advocacy, health advocacy.

Process of imagining, developing, organizing, or producing something expressive or culturally meaningful. Fine Arts. The creation or development of an artistic, educational, cultural, or expressive project; artistic or cultural production, including theater, visual art, music, writing, design, or performance.

Individuals in the Stan State community who are not or never were faculty, staff, students/alumni (might include neighbors, spouses, family members that are involved in campus). The sense of commonality felt or established in groups connected by 1) social identity or shared interest, especially non-familial group relationships, networks, professional and social networks, and collaborative communities or 2) location, especially cities and geographic communities within the six counties served by Stan State.

Growth, expansion, advancement, formation. The campus changes over the years, changes in physical structure, developments in population sizes/roles, who occupied those roles, how the university spearheaded programs for change, or how these programs developed over time. The establishment of different programs or initiatives. Expansion of the college/university. Financial Development office.  Reflection on Stan State’s growth/feel.
Delivery of university and K-12 education including teaching, curriculum, pedagogy, grading/assessment, courses, individual studies, academic standards, credential programs.
Campus landscapes, regional climate, climate change/global warming, environmental justice, flora, fauna.

Individuals holding faculty positions (new hires, lecturers, assistant, associate, and tenured professors, FERP and emeriti professors, visiting faculty, temporary/adjunct faculty, and post-doc instructors) at Stan State. Faculty participation representing Stan State (professional roles in research projects, community activities and organizations). Librarians are counted as faculty starting in 1973. Faculty union (CFA).

Individuals with legal relations to the narrator or the families of people discussed. Can include biological, adopted, in-law, surrogate, fictive, chosen, or intentional family. Discussions of upbringing.

Collegial governing of the CSU system and/or campus through the roles of the CSU Chancellor, campus presidents, provosts, and deans, as well as bodies such as the systemwide Board of Trustees, Chancellor’s Council, Academic Senate of the CSU (ASCSU), the campus academic senate, and related campus committees in the process of governing the university. The shared governing dynamic between faculty and administration (presidents, provosts, deans, etc).   Governing policies to maintain academic decrees or changes, such as requirement adjustments or degree paths. Governing policies, rules, or laws set in place for both conduct and academic discipline. Governance of broader jurisdictions (city, state, national).
Personal markers or demographics including gender, sexuality, race, ethnicity, religion, social group, class status; aspects of individuality, personality, and character.

Structures and various resources that keep Stanislaus State running including technology, resources, funding, building construction, building development, introduction of new technologies, available campus resources, mentions of funding for services, and funding for resources.
Change-oriented initiatives in any field (science and humanities).  Projects involving imagination, experimentation, innovation, or creativity.
Lasting contributions to Stan State, research, higher education, society, or humanity; reflections on university’s legacy; institutional memory; personal legacy.

Political influence, conflict, disputes, localism; relationship between university and government; partisan politics; left-center-right dynamics; Chancellors/California State university system politics; campus politics such as conflict over decisions of university presidents.

Degrees (BA/BS, MA/MS, EdD, etc), credentials, certificates, majors, minors, concentrations, or any university program meant to advance the academic progress of students. Programs initiated by Stan State or people at Stan State for academic purposes. Programs for extended education, mostly programs with a focus on academics.

The visible and meaningful presence of diverse groups of people, perspectives, and backgrounds, regardless of sex, race, religion, sexual orientation, ability, and socioeconomic status, across all levels within a system or organization (including but not limited to political representation). Demographics, diversity, internationalism, student/faculty affinity organizations, inclusion, equity.

Research, scholarship, and creativity activity by individuals or teams and/or in collaboration with other faculty, professionals, and students. Products of such research including but not limited to publications (books, journal articles, and essays), presentations, talks, exhibits, data sets, visualizations, and tools.
Service or contribution to the University or its mission, such committee work or outreach. Military or community service.

Individuals holding university staff or administrative positions (including University president, provosts, and deans), university staff experiences, staff opportunities, staff unions including California State University Employees Union (CSUEU), Teamsters Local 210, Academic Professionals of California (APC), Statewide University Police Association (SUPA), and Union of American Physicians and Dentists (UAPD).

Individuals enrolled in coursework at Stan State. Student opportunity, student experience, student relationships, student culture, student influence, student organizations, student representation, and student belonging.
Matters of labor, employment, career, professional experience, job responsibilities/duties, workplace, working conditions, unions, compensation, salary, and employment benefits/
